name: Isolated Anogenital Granulomatosis

criteria.description: Presence of non-caseating granulomatous inflammation localized to anogenital tissues on biopsy
Exclusion of infectious granulomatous diseases such as tuberculosis, syphilis, and deep fungal infections
Clinical presentation limited to anogenital region without systemic involvement
Imaging studies showing localized tissue thickening or granulomatous lesions without systemic spread

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of granulomatous inflammation in anogenital tissue plus exclusion of infectious and systemic granulomatous diseases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily one of exclusion supported by biopsy findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-caseating granulomatous inflammation localized to anogenital skin and mucosa
searchTerms: chronic granulomatous inflammation in anogenital area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent anogenital swelling with granulomatous histology

searchTerms: redness and hardening of genital skin

common.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort in anogenital area

occasional.symptomName: Fissuring or superficial erosions of anogenital skin
searchTerms: cracks or shallow sores in genital skin

occasional.symptomName: Mucosal edema causing mild functional impairment
searchTerms: swelling of mucous membranes causing mild problems
mucosal edema with slight function loss

rare.symptomName: Systemic constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: general symptoms like low fever and fatigue
scarring in genital area causing problems
anogenital scar tissue with functional issues

laboratory: Negative microbiological cultures for mycobacteria, fungi, and other infectious agents
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) may be mild or absent
imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing localized granulomatous masses or tissue thickening in anogenital region
other: Histopathology demonstrating non-caseating granulomas without necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of skip lesions on endoscopy
Positive acid-fast bacilli staining or culture
Systemic symptoms such as night sweats and weight loss
Presence of Donovan bodies on tissue smear
Ulcerative lesions with beefy red appearance

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
Failure to respond to standard immunosuppressive therapy
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th Edition. 2020.
Stern RS, et al. Granulomatous diseases of the skin. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019.
